authoritative_evidence: Civil Procedure Rules, rule 10.3(1): 'The general rule is that the period for filing an acknowledgment of service is 14 days after service of the particulars of claim.'
correct_proposition: The acknowledgment of service must be filed within 14 days after service of the particulars of claim.
false_proposition: The acknowledgment of service must be filed within 28 days after service of the particulars of claim.
question: Our client was served with the particulars of claim on 3 March. By when must the acknowledgment of service be filed?

authoritative_evidence: Civil Procedure Rules, rule 15.4(1): the defence must be filed within 14 days after service of the particulars of claim, or, 'if the defendant files an acknowledgment of service under Part 10', within 28 days after service of the particulars of claim.
correct_proposition: Because an acknowledgment of service was filed, the defence is due 28 days after service of the particulars of claim.
false_proposition: The defence is due 14 days after service of the particulars of claim regardless of the acknowledgment of service.
question: The defendant filed an acknowledgment of service. By when must the defence be filed?

authoritative_evidence: Civil Procedure Rules, rule 52.12(2)(b): where the lower court makes no other direction, the appellant's notice must be filed 'within 21 days after the date of the decision of the lower court which the appellant wishes to appeal'.
correct_proposition: The appellant's notice must be filed within 21 days of the decision.
false_proposition: The appellant's notice must be filed within 14 days of the decision.
question: The lower court gave judgment on 10 June and made no direction about time for appealing. By when must the appellant's notice be filed?

authoritative_evidence: Civil Procedure Rules, rule 7.5(1): where the claim form is to be served within the jurisdiction, the claimant must complete the relevant step required by the rule 'before 12.00 midnight on the calendar day four months after the date of issue of the claim form'.
correct_proposition: The claim form must be served within 4 months of issue.
false_proposition: The claim form must be served within 6 months of issue.
question: The claim form was issued on 1 February and is to be served within the jurisdiction. What is the period for service?

source.title: CPR Part 7 - How to Start Proceedings

authoritative_evidence: Civil Procedure Rules, rule 26.9(1): 'the small claims track is the normal track for any claim which has a financial value of not more than 10,000 pounds', subject to the special provisions about personal injury and housing disrepair claims.
correct_proposition: The normal financial limit for the small claims track is 10,000 pounds.
false_proposition: The normal financial limit for the small claims track is 15,000 pounds.
question: The claim is a straightforward debt claim with no personal injury element. What is the normal upper financial limit for allocation to the small claims track?

source.title: CPR Part 26 - Case Management: Preliminary Stage

authoritative_evidence: Civil Procedure Rules, rule 54.5(1): a claim form for judicial review must be filed 'promptly; and in any event not later than 3 months after the grounds to make the claim first arose'.
correct_proposition: The judicial review claim form must be filed promptly and in any event within 3 months of the grounds arising.
false_proposition: The judicial review claim form must be filed within 6 months of the grounds arising.
question: The decision our client wishes to challenge was made on 4 April. What is the outside time limit for filing the judicial review claim form?

authoritative_evidence: Limitation Act 1980, section 5: 'An action founded on simple contract shall not be brought after the expiration of six years from the date on which the cause of action accrued.'
correct_proposition: The limitation period for a simple contract claim is 6 years from accrual.
false_proposition: The limitation period for a simple contract claim is 12 years from accrual.
question: The alleged breach of a written but unsealed supply contract occurred on 12 January 2019. What is the limitation period?

authoritative_evidence: Limitation Act 1980, section 11(4): in an action for damages for negligence where the damages claimed consist of or include damages in respect of personal injuries, the period applicable is three years.
correct_proposition: The limitation period for a personal injury claim is 3 years.
false_proposition: The limitation period for a personal injury claim is 6 years.
question: The claimant suffered a workplace injury and had knowledge of it on the day it occurred. What is the limitation period for the personal injury claim?

authoritative_evidence: Limitation Act 1980, section 8(1): 'An action upon a specialty shall not be brought after the expiration of twelve years from the date on which the cause of action accrued.'
correct_proposition: The limitation period for an action on a deed is 12 years from accrual.
false_proposition: The limitation period for an action on a deed is 6 years from accrual.
question: The obligation our client wishes to enforce is contained in a deed. What is the limitation period?

authoritative_evidence: Limitation Act 1980, section 4A: no action for libel or slander, or for slander of title, slander of goods or other malicious falsehood, shall be brought after the expiration of one year from the date on which the cause of action accrued.
correct_proposition: The limitation period for a defamation claim is 1 year.
false_proposition: The limitation period for a defamation claim is 3 years.
question: The allegedly defamatory article was published on 2 May. What is the limitation period for the libel claim?

authoritative_evidence: Limitation Act 1980, section 15(1): 'No action shall be brought by any person to recover any land after the expiration of twelve years from the date on which the right of action accrued.'
correct_proposition: The limitation period for an action to recover land is 12 years.
false_proposition: The limitation period for an action to recover land is 20 years.
question: Our client wishes to bring an action to recover possession of unregistered land. What is the limitation period?

authoritative_evidence: Companies Act 2006, section 442(2)(a): the period allowed for delivering accounts and reports to the registrar is, for a private company, 'nine months after the end of the relevant accounting reference period'.
correct_proposition: A private company must file its annual accounts within 9 months of the end of its accounting reference period.
false_proposition: A private company must file its annual accounts within 12 months of the end of its accounting reference period.
question: The company is a private limited company whose accounting reference period ended on 31 December. By when must the accounts be delivered to the registrar?

authoritative_evidence: Companies Act 2006, section 442(2)(b): the period allowed for delivering accounts and reports to the registrar is, for a public company, 'six months after the end of the relevant accounting reference period'.
correct_proposition: A public company must file its annual accounts within 6 months of the end of its accounting reference period.
false_proposition: A public company must file its annual accounts within 9 months of the end of its accounting reference period.
question: The company is a public limited company. By when must its accounts be delivered to the registrar?

authoritative_evidence: Companies Act 2006, section 853A(1): a company must deliver a confirmation statement to the registrar before the end of the period of 14 days after the end of each review period.
correct_proposition: The confirmation statement must be delivered within 14 days after the end of the review period.
false_proposition: The confirmation statement must be delivered within 28 days after the end of the review period.
question: The company's review period ended on 30 September. By when must the confirmation statement be delivered to Companies House?

authoritative_evidence: Companies Act 2006, section 859A(4): the period allowed for delivering a charge for registration is '21 days beginning with the day after the date of creation of the charge'.
correct_proposition: A charge must be delivered to the registrar for registration within 21 days beginning with the day after its creation.
false_proposition: A charge must be delivered to the registrar for registration within 28 days beginning with the day after its creation.
question: The company granted a debenture on 5 August. By when must the charge be delivered to Companies House for registration?

authoritative_evidence: Companies Act 2006, section 555(3): a company must deliver the return of allotment of shares to the registrar 'within one month of making the allotment'.
correct_proposition: The return of allotment must be delivered to the registrar within one month of the allotment.
false_proposition: The return of allotment must be delivered to the registrar within 14 days of the allotment.
question: The company allotted new ordinary shares on 7 July. By when must the return of allotment be delivered to Companies House?

authoritative_evidence: Companies Act 2006, section 283(1): 'A special resolution of the members (or of a class of members) of a company means a resolution passed by a majority of not less than 75%.'
correct_proposition: A special resolution requires a majority of not less than 75%.
false_proposition: A special resolution requires a majority of not less than two-thirds.
question: The board wishes to amend the company's articles by special resolution. What majority is required?

authoritative_evidence: Employment Rights Act 1996, section 111(2)(a): an employment tribunal shall not consider a complaint of unfair dismissal unless it is presented 'before the end of the period of three months beginning with the effective date of termination'.
correct_proposition: The unfair dismissal claim must be presented within 3 months beginning with the effective date of termination.
false_proposition: The unfair dismissal claim must be presented within 6 months beginning with the effective date of termination.
question: The employee's effective date of termination was 1 April. Ignoring any ACAS early conciliation extension, what is the primary time limit for presenting the unfair dismissal claim?

authoritative_evidence: Employment Rights Act 1996, section 108(1): the right not to be unfairly dismissed 'does not apply to the dismissal of an employee unless he has been continuously employed for a period of not less than two years ending with the effective date of termination'.
correct_proposition: The qualifying period for ordinary unfair dismissal is 2 years of continuous employment.
false_proposition: The qualifying period for ordinary unfair dismissal is 1 year of continuous employment.
question: The employee was dismissed for poor performance in 2026 and alleges ordinary unfair dismissal. What period of continuous employment is required to bring the claim?
note: The Employment Rights Act 2025 reduces this qualifying period from two years to six months. The Government has stated its intention to commence that change on 1 January 2027, so this ground truth is correct for dismissals with an effective date of termination before then.

authoritative_evidence: Employment Rights Act 1996, section 86(1)(b): the notice required to be given by an employer to terminate the contract of an employee who has been continuously employed for two years or more is 'one week's notice for each year of continuous employment if his period of continuous employment is less than twelve years', and section 86(1)(c) provides for 'not less than twelve weeks' notice' where the period is twelve years or more.
correct_proposition: The statutory minimum notice an employer must give is capped at 12 weeks.
false_proposition: The statutory minimum notice an employer must give is capped at 8 weeks.
question: The employee has 15 years' continuous service. What is the maximum statutory minimum notice the employer must give?

authoritative_evidence: Employment Rights Act 1996, section 155: 'An employee does not have any right to a redundancy payment unless he has been continuously employed for a period of not less than two years ending with the relevant date.'
correct_proposition: The qualifying period for a statutory redundancy payment is 2 years of continuous employment.
false_proposition: The qualifying period for a statutory redundancy payment is 1 year of continuous employment.
question: The employee's role is being made redundant. What period of continuous employment is required to qualify for a statutory redundancy payment?

authoritative_evidence: Employment Rights Act 1996, section 1(2), as amended with effect from 6 April 2020: the written statement of employment particulars 'shall be given not later than the beginning of the employment'.
correct_proposition: The written statement of particulars must be given no later than the first day of employment.
false_proposition: The written statement of particulars must be given within 2 months of the start of employment.
question: A new employee started on 1 September 2026. By when must the written statement of employment particulars be given?

authoritative_evidence: Maternity and Parental Leave etc. Regulations 1999: an employee is entitled to 26 weeks' ordinary maternity leave under regulation 7(1) and to 26 weeks' additional maternity leave under regulation 6(1)(b), giving a total entitlement of 52 weeks.
correct_proposition: The total statutory maternity leave entitlement is 52 weeks.
false_proposition: The total statutory maternity leave entitlement is 39 weeks.
question: An employee is taking her full statutory maternity leave. What is the total leave entitlement?

source.title: Maternity and Parental Leave etc. Regulations 1999

authoritative_evidence: Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013, regulation 30(2)-(3): for a sales contract the cancellation period ends at the end of 14 days after the day on which the goods come into the physical possession of the consumer.
correct_proposition: The consumer has 14 days from receipt of the goods to cancel the distance contract.
false_proposition: The consumer has 7 days from receipt of the goods to cancel the distance contract.
question: A consumer bought goods from our client's website and received them on 10 October. What is the cancellation period?

source.title: Consumer Contracts (Information, Cancellation and Additional Charges) Regulations 2013

authoritative_evidence: Consumer Rights Act 2015, section 22(3): the time limit for exercising the short-term right to reject goods that do not conform to the contract 'is the end of 30 days beginning with the first day after' ownership has transferred, the goods have been delivered and any required installation is done.
correct_proposition: The short-term right to reject faulty goods lasts 30 days.
false_proposition: The short-term right to reject faulty goods lasts 14 days.
question: A consumer took delivery of a faulty appliance. How long is the short-term right to reject?

authoritative_evidence: Consumer Rights Act 2015, section 19(14)-(15): goods which do not conform to the contract at any time within the period of six months beginning with the day on which they were delivered are to be taken not to have conformed on that day, subject to the exceptions in subsection (15).
correct_proposition: The burden of proof is reversed in the consumer's favour for 6 months after delivery.
false_proposition: The burden of proof is reversed in the consumer's favour for 12 months after delivery.
question: A consumer complains of a fault four months after delivery and the trader disputes that the fault was present at delivery. For how long does the statutory presumption operate in the consumer's favour?

authoritative_evidence: UK GDPR, Article 33(1): in the case of a personal data breach, the controller shall notify the personal data breach to the Information Commissioner 'without undue delay and, where feasible, not later than 72 hours after having become aware of it', unless the breach is unlikely to result in a risk to the rights and freedoms of natural persons.
correct_proposition: A notifiable personal data breach must be reported to the ICO within 72 hours of the controller becoming aware of it.
false_proposition: A notifiable personal data breach must be reported to the ICO within 7 days of the controller becoming aware of it.
question: Our client became aware of a notifiable personal data breach at 09:00 on Monday. By when must it notify the ICO?

authoritative_evidence: UK GDPR, Article 12(3): the controller shall provide information on action taken on a request under Articles 15 to 22 'without undue delay and in any event within one month of receipt of the request', extendable by two further months where necessary taking into account the complexity and number of requests.
correct_proposition: A subject access request must ordinarily be answered within one month of receipt.
false_proposition: A subject access request must ordinarily be answered within 40 days of receipt.
question: Our client received a subject access request on 3 March and the request is not complex. What is the response deadline?

authoritative_evidence: Finance Act 2003, section 76(1) as amended by the Finance Act 2019: a land transaction return must be delivered to HMRC 'before the end of the period of 14 days after the effective date of the transaction'.
correct_proposition: The SDLT return must be delivered within 14 days of the effective date of the transaction.
false_proposition: The SDLT return must be delivered within 30 days of the effective date of the transaction.
question: Completion of the purchase took place on 6 May 2026. By when must the SDLT return be delivered to HMRC?

authoritative_evidence: HMRC guidance on VAT thresholds: a business must register for VAT if its VAT taxable turnover goes over the registration threshold of 90,000 pounds, which has applied since 1 April 2024.
correct_proposition: The VAT registration threshold is 90,000 pounds of taxable turnover.
false_proposition: The VAT registration threshold is 85,000 pounds of taxable turnover.
question: Our client's rolling 12-month taxable turnover is approaching the registration threshold. What is the current threshold?
